resources.string: OpenAver now runs entirely on this device. Scan videos from real phone storage, manage metadata, and play them without connecting to a PC or NAS.
OpenAver needs “All files access” so it can scan video folders, read NFO and cover files, rename files, and write metadata beside your videos. Nothing is uploaded to this app’s developer.
All files access is required before the local scanner can start.
All files access is enabled. Starting the local server…
Could not open the system permission page. Open Android Settings → Apps → OpenAver Mobile → Permissions manually.
Android’s special all-files permission lets OpenAver use normal file paths instead of opaque document URIs.
On Scanner, tap the folder button and browse to /storage/emulated/0 or your SD card, then choose the folder containing videos.
Generation, metadata search, NFO/cover writes, and playback all run on the phone. Network access is only used for metadata sources you enable.
The Python server, SQLite database, logs, and generated data stay inside this app’s private storage. Video files remain in their original phone folders.
